parts.label: (a)(i)
key_concepts: amplitude as maximum displacement from equilibrium
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 4.2 for the first few oscillations - find the middle line the oscillation is centred on and the highest and lowest values of $L$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find the equilibrium position**
Think of amplitude as how far you pull the trolley away from where it would sit at rest. On the $L$-$t$ graph the oscillation is centred on $L = 20\text{ cm}$, swinging between $25\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$.

Step 2: **Calculate the distance from centre to extreme**
$$x_0 = L_{max} - L_{eq} = 25 - 20 = 5.0\text{ cm}$$ This is the same as half the peak-to-peak height. So the initial amplitude is $5.0\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the undamped part at the start of Fig. 4.2 - measure the time for one complete repeat, e.g. from one peak at $t = 0$ to the next peak.
Hint 2: Recall how angular frequency links to period for any sinusoidal oscillation and check your units are $\text{rad s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the period from the graph**
You are sitting with the $L$-$t$ curve. Peaks occur at $t = 0, 4.0, 8.0, 12.0\text{ s}$. The time between successive peaks is constant:
$$T = 4.0\text{ s}$$

Step 2: **Convert period to angular frequency**
Angular frequency tells you how many radians of the cycle are covered per second:
$$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{4.0}$$
$$\omega = 1.6\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
key_concepts: maximum speed in SHM v0 = omega x0
hints: Hint 1: Remember that speed is greatest as the trolley rushes through the equilibrium position, and it depends on both how wide and how fast the oscillation is.
Hint 2: Combine your values of amplitude $x_0$ and angular frequency $\omega$ from (i) and (ii), keeping distance in $\text{cm}$ so the speed comes out in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Use the SHM maximum speed rule**
For simple harmonic motion the maximum speed is at the centre and is given by:
$$v_0 = \omega x_0$$ where $x_0$ is the amplitude.

Step 2: **Substitute your numbers**
$$v_0 = 1.57 \times 5.0$$
$$v_0 = 7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$ Keep $x_0$ in cm to get $v_0$ directly in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ as requested.

parts.label: (b)
key_concepts: effect of friction when air cushion removed
hints: Hint 1: Compare the starting value $L = 25\text{ cm}$ with the centre value $L = 20\text{ cm}$ - which side was the trolley pulled to?
Hint 2: Look at how the height of the peaks changes before $t = 12\text{ s}$ and after $t = 12\text{ s}$ - when is amplitude constant and when does it shrink?
Hint 3: Link the change at about $12\text{ s}$ to the story in the stem about the air blower being switched off - what type of damping does this produce?
parts.proper_answer: Trolley initially pulled to right of equilibrium position at $L = 20\text{ cm}$. From 0 to 12 s motion is undamped SHM with constant amplitude and period 4.0 s. From 12 s motion is lightly damped with decreasing amplitude.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the starting position**
At $t = 0$, $L = 25\text{ cm}$ which is $5\text{ cm}$ to the right of the equilibrium $L = 20\text{ cm}$. So you pulled it to the Y side and let go from rest.

Step 2: **Spot undamped then damped behaviour**
From $t = 0$ to $t = 12\text{ s}$ the peaks stay at $25\text{ cm}$ and troughs at $15\text{ cm}$. Constant amplitude means no energy loss - free undamped SHM on the air cushion with period $4.0\text{ s}$.

Step 3: **Explain the later decay**
After about $t = 12\text{ s}$ the amplitude steadily falls. This is when the blower is switched off, the trolley touches the track and friction removes energy. The amplitude falls gradually and the period stays about the same, so this is light damping.

parts.label: (c)
hints: Hint 1: Think about what $v$ must be at the turning points $L = 15\text{ cm}$ and $25\text{ cm}$, and where $|v|$ must be largest.
Hint 2: Use your values from (a) to mark the left-right limits of $L$ and the top-bottom limits of $v$ on Fig. 4.3.
Hint 3: Remember the trolley starts at $L = 25\text{ cm}$ and moves to smaller $L$, so the first velocity must be negative - join the points into a smooth closed loop centred on $(20,0)$.
parts.proper_answer: Closed elliptical loop centred on $(20\text{ cm}, 0)$, extending from $L = 15\text{ cm}$ to $25\text{ cm}$ and from $v = -7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to $+7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$, starting at $(25,0)$ going negative.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify the key points of the loop**
At the extremes $L = 15\text{ cm}$ and $L = 25\text{ cm}$ the trolley momentarily stops, so $v = 0$. At the centre $L = 20\text{ cm}$ speed is maximum, $v = \pm 7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$. A $v$-$L$ plot for undamped SHM is therefore a closed ellipse centred on $(20,0)$.

Step 2: **Get the direction correct**
At $t = 0$ you are at $(25,0)$. Just after release $L$ decreases, so $v$ is negative. That means you leave the right-hand point and go downwards. You pass through $(20, -7.9)$ at maximum speed leftwards, round to $(15,0)$, back through $(20, +7.9)$ and return to $(25,0)$ after one period.

Step 3: **Sketch to scale**
Draw a smooth symmetric ellipse with $L_{min} = 15\text{ cm}$, $L_{max} = 25\text{ cm}$, $v_{min} = -7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$, $v_{max} = +7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$. Only the first oscillation is needed, so a single closed loop with no decay.
